_comment: The module's worked example: one real patent, forty scores, seven company figures.
Notebooks 3 and 4 read this file, so the example exists once and cannot drift.
V5 settled on TIP 2026-08-15: EP3074539B1, Q-Linea AB. Chosen out of 135 candidates in
module 5's antibiotic-resistance corpus because Q-Linea really does the AMR rapid testing
this example used to invent, and because its legal history teaches the point of the
evidence layer: granted and unopposed, designated in 38 EPC states, in force in four.
!! THE FINANCIAL FIGURES ARE ILLUSTRATIVE AND ARE NOT Q-LINEA'S ACCOUNTS. !!
Turnover, cost structure and depreciation are not in PATSTAT and were never looked up.
They are a plausible mid-size diagnostics company, chosen so the cash-flow chart teaches
well - the technology reaches the market early enough and lives long enough to fill the
ten-year horizon with all six components non-zero. Every artifact that shows them must
say so; see 'financials_note' below, which the report prints verbatim.
The forty scores are THE ADVISER'S FIRST PASS - what a person would write down before
checking anything. They are deliberately left uncorrected: 2_evidence_from_patstat.ipynb
measures what PATSTAT can decide and writes the corrected set to its own output folder,
and the difference between the two is the module's whole argument. Do not 'fix' a score
here because the data disagrees with it - that disagreement is the deliverable.

patent.title: Method for detecting and characterising a microorganism

financials_note: Illustrative figures for a mid-size diagnostics company - NOT Q-Linea AB's accounts. PATSTAT holds no financial data; these were chosen to make the model legible and must not be read as anything about the real company.
